$comment: Attachments referenced by the rest of the package. The `provides` key names the attachment label a clause supplies; validate.mjs and the in-app consistency checker both use it to prove that every 'Schedule A' or 'Exhibit B' reference has something behind it.

clauses.title: Schedule A — Ownership, Contributions, and Notice Addresses
clauses.rationale: Carries the numbers that would otherwise force an amendment every time the cap table moves, and the addresses the notice provision depends on.
clauses.body: For each of {{founderList}}: full legal name, mailing address and email for notices, initial contribution, and ownership percentage. Percentages must total one hundred percent (100%). {{ownerSplitNote}} This schedule is referenced by <<xr:gov_units>> and supplies the notice addresses used throughout the package. Update it — rather than the body of the {{govDoc}} — on any permitted transfer or new issuance.

clauses.title: Exhibit A — Prior Inventions
clauses.rationale: A blank exhibit is itself the representation that no prior inventions are excluded, which is why it must exist even when there is nothing to list.
clauses.body: Each founder lists here any invention created before the Effective Date that they wish to exclude from the assignment in <<xr:ipa_assign>>, with enough detail to identify it without disclosing the substance of any trade secret. A founder with nothing to list should write “None” and sign — leaving this exhibit blank and unsigned creates ambiguity about whether it was ever completed.

clauses.title: Exhibit B — Spousal Consent
clauses.rationale: Supplies the attachment the spousal consent clause refers to. Without it that clause points at a document that does not exist.
clauses.body: The spouse of each married {{ownerSing}} acknowledges having read the {{govDoc}}, consents to its terms, and agrees that any community property interest in the {{ownerSing}}’s ownership is bound by the transfer restrictions and buy-sell provisions it contains. This exhibit supports <<xr:gov_spousal>>.
